title: Further local object pagination optimization

requirements.LOO01: Find and implement measured further improvements to the linear local cleanup scan.
requirements.LOO02: Retain current cursor compatibility, current type/age/reference/pin checks, guarded uploads and bounded memory.
requirements.LOO03: Separate operation-count improvements from unmeasured NAS wall-time claims.

outcome: Implemented fewer startup metadata operations, name-only manifest preparation, a bounded 256 KiB sequential write buffer, path-object reuse with fresh directory checks, and removal of the explicit next-page read probe. Manifest layout, cursor format and object paths remain unchanged.
changes: Startup still visits at most 1000 directory entries, but filters temporary-upload names before fetching metadata. Ordinary objects no longer cause file stat and per-object parent-link checks during startup.

Preparation records validated candidate names without calling DirEntry.is_file. Current file type is still checked when each page is consumed. A directory or link with an object-shaped name can be a manifest candidate but cannot become an eligible object row.
Manifest preparation uses one bounded 262144-byte write buffer and a streaming writelines generator. It retains flush/fsync and atomic publication; no unbounded filename collection is introduced.
Adjacent candidates in one shard reuse the same Path object, but the actual directory-link check is repeated for every candidate. No cached safety verdict is reused.

Page continuation compares its final byte offset with the already-fstat'ed immutable manifest length. It avoids an explicit read solely to detect a following page. The buffered IO implementation may still prefetch normally.

measurements.scope: Instrumented application metadata requests and raw writes, synthetic directory entries with real manifest files. The host is Windows Python 3.14.7 with a 131072-byte default buffer. A separate explicit 8192-byte profile models the deployment Python 3.12 buffer. These counts do not claim equivalent wall-time or NAS throughput gains.
measurements.qualification: DirEntry.is_file can use cached directory metadata on actual filesystems. Eliminating its calls does not universally eliminate the same number of OS syscalls. The fresh page-time file stat and directory guard remain.
measurements.rejected_compact_encoding_probe: A prototype Base64 digest format reduced 100000 ordinary records from 7300000 to 4500000 bytes, but median encoding-only CPU time increased from 0.0309 to 0.1370 seconds on this host. It was not implemented: this slice preserves byte layout and avoids that additional CPU/versioning cost. These isolated encoder numbers are not whole-scan timings.

complexity_and_limits.complete_scan: Still O(n) directory work and O(k) page work; n is directory entries and k is at most 1000 candidates. This slice reduces constant factors.
complexity_and_limits.memory: O(k) plus a fixed 256 KiB manifest write buffer; at most one builder per local root is active.
complexity_and_limits.disk_and_preparation: The first streaming preparation pass and roughly 73 bytes per ordinary object are unchanged. Crash-interrupted preparation still restarts its enumeration.
complexity_and_limits.further_architecture: Reducing routine cleanup to changed objects would require a durable upload/delete inventory plus crash reconciliation and periodic filesystem discovery of untracked files. That is a larger write-path and rollout change, not part of this optimization.
remaining_acceptance: Representative NAS/Linux latency, memory and free-space measurements

validation.skip: The SQLite instance of the publication/GC race requires PostgreSQL row locks. PostgreSQL parametrizations and live GCS contracts were explicitly deselected.

pin/reference protection and active upload guards
startup performs no ordinary-file stats while retaining its 1000-entry limit
preparation does not fetch per-entry file types
directory guard is rechecked for adjacent candidates sharing one Path
